metadata.title: From finite-system entropy to entropy rate for a Hidden Markov Process

extraction_notes.note: Lemma 1 states F_N([\epsilon]_1^N) = F_{N-j+1}([\epsilon]_{j+1}^N), but its proof ends with a sum over [Z]_j^N and the proof of Lemma 3 applies it as F_{N-j+1}([\epsilon]_j^N); the index j+1 looks like a typo for j (a vector of length N-j+1 starts at j).

Eq. (11) writes C_N^{(k)} as the plain sum of F_N^{\vec k} over weight-k vectors; the Taylor coefficient of the diagonal restriction carries a factor 1/(k_1!...k_N!), which is missing (the termwise argument of the main proof is unaffected). The claim is stated without argument (rigor semi_formal).

Typos copied verbatim: conditional entropy written with P(U=u) instead of P(V=v); 'the signal to noise ratio (SNR) is small' where the next sentence treats the high-SNR (small-noise) regime; t_{X_i r} in Lemmas 2-3 has an index i not bound there (should involve the differentiated site).

The proof of Theorem 1 is a \begin{proof} environment placed after Lemma 3, introduced by 'We are now ready to prove our main theorem:' (no syntactic link); its proves edge was added as named. A stray \label{strong_thm} follows it and is never referenced.

Each lemma's proof sits inside the lemma environment, with the lemma's \label after \end{proof}; latex_facts attributes the label to the proof, so the \ref edges run from the proofs (PP1->PP2, PP3->PP4, ...) and into the lemma nodes whose statements contain the next proof. Named edges from the lemmas themselves were added to the citing steps.

The conjecture of [ZKD1] that the theorem generalizes is mentioned but never stated, so it has no node; the abstract, the history paragraph of the introduction and the first summarizing sentence of the conclusion are discussion.

metadata.extraction_comment: The main theorem assumes (footnote) uniform analyticity of C_N in a common neighbourhood of epsilon=0; this assumption is not proven in the paper and is recorded among the theorem's assumptions.

nodes.name: Markov process and its noisy observation
nodes.statement: \PARstart{L}{et} $\{X_N\}$ be a finite state stationary Markov process over the alphabet $\Sigma = \{1,..,s\}$, and let $\{Y_N\}$ be its noisy observation (on the same alphabet).
nodes.statement_short: $X$ is a finite-state stationary Markov process on $\Sigma=\{1,..,s\}$ and $Y$ its noisy observation.

nodes.name: Transition matrix and emission matrix
nodes.statement: The pair can be described by the Markov transition matrix $M = M_{s \times s} = \{m_{ij}\}$ and the emission matrix $R = R_{s\times s}$, which yield the probabilities $P(X_{N+1} = j | X_N = i) = m_{ij}$ and $P(Y_N = j | X_N = i) = r_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_short: $M=\{m_{ij}\}$ is the Markov transition matrix and $R=\{r_{ij}\}$ the emission matrix.

nodes.name: Small-noise regime and strictly positive transition matrix
nodes.statement: We consider here the case where the signal to noise ratio (SNR) is small and $M$ is strictly positive ($m_{ij} > 0$) and thus has a unique stationary distribution.

nodes.name: High-SNR parametrization R = I + epsilon T
nodes.statement: For the `high - SNR' regime one may write $R = I + \epsilon T$, where $\epsilon > 0$ is some small number, $I$ is the identity matrix, and the matrix $T = \{t_{ij}\}$ satisfies $t_{ii} < 0, \: t_{ij} \geq 0 , \: \forall i \neq j$ and $\sum_{j=1}^{s}{t_{ij}} = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: In the high-SNR regime the emission matrix is $R=I+\epsilon T$ with small $\epsilon>0$ and $T$ a rate-like matrix (rows sum to 0).

nodes.name: Hidden Markov Process (HMP)
nodes.statement: The process $Y$ can be viewed as an observation of $X$ through a noisy channel. It is an example of a {\it Hidden Markov Process (HMP)}, and is determined by the parameters $M$, $T$ and $\epsilon$.
nodes.genus: observation of $X$ through a noisy channel

nodes.name: Vector notation [X]_i^j
nodes.statement: More formally, for $i \leq j$ let $[X]_i^j$ denote the vector $(X_i,..,X_j)$.

nodes.name: Shannon entropy rate
nodes.statement: The entropy rate is defined as: \begin{equation} \bar{H}(Y) = \lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{H([Y]_1^N)}{N} \end{equation} \noindent Where $H(X) = -\sum_X P(X) \log P(X)$; We will sometimes omit the realization $x$ of the variable $X$, so $P(X)$ should be understood as $P(X = x)$.
nodes.statement_short: The entropy rate is $\bar H(Y)=\lim_N H([Y]_1^N)/N$, with $H$ the Shannon entropy.

nodes.name: Entropy rate as limit of conditional entropy
nodes.statement: For a stationary process the limit in (\ref{entropy_rate_def}) exists and $\bar{H}$ can also be computed via the conditional entropy (\cite{Cover}) as: $\bar{H}(Y) = \lim_{N \to \infty} H(Y_N | [Y]_1^{N-1})$.
conclusions: $\bar{H}$ can also be computed via the conditional entropy (\cite{Cover}) as: $\bar{H}(Y) = \lim_{N \to \infty} H(Y_N | [Y]_1^{N-1})$
nodes.statement_short: For a stationary process the entropy rate exists and equals $\lim_N H(Y_N|[Y]_1^{N-1})$.

nodes.name: Conditional entropy
nodes.statement: Here $H(U|V)$ represents the conditional entropy, which for random variables $U$ and $V$ is the average uncertainty of the conditional distribution of $U$ conditioned on $V$, that is $H(U|V) = \sum_{v} P(U = u) H(U | V=v) $.
nodes.genus: the average uncertainty of the conditional distribution of $U$ conditioned on $V$

nodes.name: Chain rule for entropy
nodes.statement: By the chain rule for entropy, it can also be viewed as a difference of entropies, $H(U|V) = H(U,V) - H(V)$.

nodes.name: Explicit expression for the entropy rate of an HMP
nodes.statement: There is at present no explicit expression for the entropy rate of a {\it HMP} (\cite{Merhav,Jacquet}).

nodes.name: Entropy rate definition
nodes.statement: \bar{H}(Y) = \lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{H([Y]_1^N)}{N}
nodes.label: entropy_rate_def

nodes.name: Settling of the entropy-rate expansion coefficients
nodes.statement: Let $H_N \equiv H_N(M,T,\epsilon) = H([Y]_1^N)$ be the entropy of a system of length $N$, and let $C_N = H_N - H_{N-1}$. Assume\footnote{\noindent It is easy to show that the functions $C_N$ are differentiable to all orders in $\epsilon$, at $\epsilon =0$. The assumption which is not proven here is that they are in fact analytic with a radius of analyticity which is uniform in $N$, and are uniformly bounded within some common neighborhood of $\epsilon =0$} there is some (complex) neighborhood $B_{\rho}(0) \subset \mathbb{C}$ of zero, in which the (one-variable) functions $\{ C_N \}$ and $\bar{H}$ are analytic in $\epsilon$, with a Taylor expansion given by: \begin{equation} C_N(M,T,\epsilon) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} C_N^{(k)} \epsilon^k, \quad \bar{H}(M,T,\epsilon) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} C^{(k)} \epsilon^k \end{equation} \noindent (The coefficients $C_N^{(k)}$ are functions of the parameters $M$ and $T$. From now on we omit this dependence). Then: \begin{equation} N \geq \lceil \frac{k+3}{2} \rceil \Rightarrow C_N^{(k)} = C^{(k)} \end{equation}
assumptions: $H_N \equiv H_N(M,T,\epsilon) = H([Y]_1^N)$ be the entropy of a system of length $N$
there is some (complex) neighborhood $B_{\rho}(0) \subset \mathbb{C}$ of zero, in which the (one-variable) functions $\{ C_N \}$ and $\bar{H}$ are analytic in $\epsilon$
also_stated_at: The surprising 'settling' of the expansion coefficients $C_N^{(k)} = C^{(k)}$ for $N \geq \lceil \frac{k+3}{2} \rceil$, hold for the entropy.
nodes.statement_short: If $C_N=H_N-H_{N-1}$ and $\bar H$ are analytic in $\epsilon$ near 0 (uniformly), the $k$-th Taylor coefficient of $C_N$ equals that of the entropy rate once $N\ge\lceil (k+3)/2\rceil$.
nodes.label: main_thm

nodes.name: Taylor expansions of C_N and the entropy rate
nodes.statement: C_N(M,T,\epsilon) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} C_N^{(k)} \epsilon^k, \quad \bar{H}(M,T,\epsilon) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} C^{(k)} \epsilon^k

nodes.name: Settling of the coefficients
nodes.statement: N \geq \lceil \frac{k+3}{2} \rceil \Rightarrow C_N^{(k)} = C^{(k)}

nodes.name: C_N is an upper bound for the entropy rate
nodes.statement: \noindent $C_N$ is an upperbound (\cite{Cover}) for $\bar{H}$.

nodes.name: Earlier symbolic discovery and k <= 2 proof
nodes.statement: The behavior stated in Thm. \ref{main_thm} was discovered using symbolic computations, but proven only for $k \leq 2$ , in the binary symmetric case (\cite{ZKD1}).

nodes.name: Process Z with site-dependent noise
nodes.statement: We consider a more general process $\{Z_N\}$, where $Z_i$'s emission matrix is $R_i = I + \epsilon_iT$. The process $\{Z_N\}$ is determined by $M$,$T$ and $[\epsilon]_{1}^N$.

nodes.name: Functions F_N
nodes.statement: We define the following functions: \begin{equation} F_N(M,T,[\epsilon]_1^{N}) = H([Z]_1^N) - H([Z]_1^{N-1}) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $F_N$ is the entropy increment $H([Z]_1^N)-H([Z]_1^{N-1})$ of the site-dependent-noise process.

nodes.name: F_N on the diagonal equals C_N
nodes.statement: Setting all the $\epsilon_i$'s equal reduces us back to the $Y$ process, so in particular $F_N(M,T, (\epsilon,..,\epsilon)) = C_N(\epsilon)$.

nodes.name: Blocking observation
nodes.statement: Second, we observe that if a particular $\epsilon_i$ is set to zero, the observation $Z_i$ equals the state $X_i$. Thus, conditioning back to the past is 'blocked'.
assumptions: a particular $\epsilon_i$ is set to zero
conclusions: conditioning back to the past is 'blocked'
nodes.statement_short: If $\epsilon_i=0$ then $Z_i=X_i$, so by the Markov property conditioning on the past is blocked at site $i$.

nodes.name: Blocking lemma
nodes.statement_short: A zero noise parameter at site $j$ cuts $F_N$ down to $F_{N-j+1}$ of the sites after $j$.

nodes.name: Proof of the blocking lemma
nodes.statement_short: Write $F_N$ as a conditional entropy and use the Markov property: $Z_j=X_j$ blocks conditioning on sites before $j$.
nodes.label: F_cond_lemma

nodes.name: Blocking of conditioning
nodes.statement: \epsilon_j = 0 \Rightarrow P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1}) = P(Z_N | [Z]_j^{N-1})
nodes.label: blocking_cond

nodes.name: Write F_N as a conditional-entropy sum
nodes.statement: $F$ can be written as the sum: \begin{equation} F_N = -\sum_{[Z]_1^N} P([Z]_1^{N-1}) P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1}) \log P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1}) \end{equation} \noindent Here the dependence on $[\epsilon]_1^N$ and $M,T$ is hidden in the probabilities $P(..)$.
nodes.statement_short: Write F_N as a conditional-entropy sum

nodes.name: Markov property blocks conditioning at site j
nodes.statement: Since $\epsilon_j=0$, we must have $X_j = Z_j$, and therefore (since $X$ is a Markov chain), conditioning further to the past is 'blocked', that is: \begin{equation} \epsilon_j = 0 \Rightarrow P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1}) = P(Z_N | [Z]_j^{N-1}) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Markov property blocks conditioning at site j

nodes.name: Substitute and marginalize to get F_{N-j+1}
nodes.statement: Substituting in eq. \ref{F_cond_eq} gives: $$ F_N = -\sum_{[Z]_1^N} P([Z]_1^{N-1}) P(Z_N | [Z]_j^{N-1}) \log P(Z_N | [Z]_j^{N-1}) = $$ \begin{equation} -\sum_{[Z]_{j}^N} P([Z]_j^{N}) \log P(Z_N | [Z]_j^{N-1}) = F_{N-j+1} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Substitute and marginalize to get F_{N-j+1}

nodes.name: Derivative-order vector k
nodes.statement: \noindent Let $\vec{k} = [k]_1^N$ be a vector with $k_i \in \{\mathbb{N} \cup 0\}$.

nodes.name: Weight of k
nodes.statement: Define its 'weight' as $\omega(\vec{k}) = \sum_{i=1}^N k_i$.

nodes.name: Mixed derivatives F_N^k at zero noise
nodes.statement: Define also: \begin{equation} F_N^{\vec{k}} \equiv \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})} F_N}{\partial \epsilon_1^{k_1},..,\partial \epsilon_N^{k_N}} \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $F_N^{\vec k}$ is the mixed partial derivative of $F_N$ of orders $k_i$ in $\epsilon_i$, at $\vec\epsilon=0$.

nodes.name: Definition of F_N^k
nodes.statement: F_N^{\vec{k}} \equiv \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})} F_N}{\partial \epsilon_1^{k_1},..,\partial \epsilon_N^{k_N}} \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0}

nodes.name: Leading zeros leave F_N^k unchanged
nodes.statement: Let $\vec{k} = [k]_1^N$ with $k_1 \leq 1$. Denote $\vec{k}^{(r)}$ the concatenation: $\vec{k}^{(r)} = (\underbrace{0,..,0}_r,k_1,..,k_N)$. Then: $$ F_N^{\vec{k}} = F_{r+N}^{\vec{k}^{(r)}} \quad, \forall r \in \mathbb{N} $$ \begin{proof} \noindent Assume first $k_1 = 0$. Using lemma \ref{F_cond_lemma}, we get: $$ F_{N+r}^{\vec{k}^{(r)}}([\epsilon]_1^{N+r}) = \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k}^{(r)})} F_{r+N}([\epsilon]_1^{N+r})}{\partial \epsilon_{r+2}^{k_2},..,\partial \epsilon_{r+N}^{k_N}} \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = $$ \begin{equation} \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})} F_{N}([\epsilon]_{r+1}^{N+r})}{\partial \epsilon_{r+2}^{k_2},..,\partial \epsilon_{r+N}^{k_N}} \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = F_N^{\vec{k}}([\epsilon]_{r+1}^{r+N}) \end{equation} \noindent The case $k_1 = 1$ is reduced back to the case $k_1=0$ by taking the derivative. We denote ${[Z]_1^N}^{(j \to r)}$ the vector which is equal to $[Z]_1^N$ in all coordinates except on coordinate $j$, where $Z_j = r$. Using eq. \ref{k_is_zero_eq}, we get: $$ F_{N+1}^{\vec{k}^{(1)}}([\epsilon]_1^{N+1}) = \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_3^{k_2} \dots \partial \epsilon_{N+1}^{k_N}} \left[ \left. \frac{\partial F_{N+1}}{\partial \epsilon_2} \right|_{\epsilon_2 = 0} \right] \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = $$ $$ \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_3^{k_2} \dots \partial \epsilon_{N+1}^{k_N}} \Biggl\{ - \sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} \sum_{[Z]_1^{N+1}} $$ $$ \left[ P({[Z]_1^{N+1}}^{(2 \to r)}) \log P(Z_{N+1} | [Z]_1^{N}) - \right. $$ $$ \left. \left. \left. P(Z_{N+1} | [Z]_1^{N}) P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(2 \to r)}) \right] \right|_{\epsilon_2 = 0} \Biggr\} \right|_{[\epsilon]_1^{N+1} = 0} = $$ $$ \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_2^{k_2} \dots \partial \epsilon_{N}^{k_N}} \Biggl\{ - \sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} \sum_{[Z]_1^{N}} $$ $$ \left[ P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(1 \to r)}) \log P(Z_{N} | [Z]_1^{N-1}) - \right. $$ \begin{equation} \left. \left. \left. P(Z_{N} | [Z]_1^{N-1}) P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(1 \to r)}) \right] \right|_{\epsilon_1 = 0} \Biggr\} \right|_{[\epsilon]_1^{N} = 0} = F_{N}^{\vec{k}}([\epsilon]_1^{N})\end{equation} \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Padding $\vec k$ (with $k_1\le 1$) by $r$ leading zeros does not change $F_N^{\vec k}$.

nodes.name: Proof that leading zeros leave F_N^k unchanged
nodes.statement: \noindent Assume first $k_1 = 0$. Using lemma \ref{F_cond_lemma}, we get: $$ F_{N+r}^{\vec{k}^{(r)}}([\epsilon]_1^{N+r}) = \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k}^{(r)})} F_{r+N}([\epsilon]_1^{N+r})}{\partial \epsilon_{r+2}^{k_2},..,\partial \epsilon_{r+N}^{k_N}} \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = $$ \begin{equation} \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})} F_{N}([\epsilon]_{r+1}^{N+r})}{\partial \epsilon_{r+2}^{k_2},..,\partial \epsilon_{r+N}^{k_N}} \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = F_N^{\vec{k}}([\epsilon]_{r+1}^{r+N}) \end{equation} \noindent The case $k_1 = 1$ is reduced back to the case $k_1=0$ by taking the derivative. We denote ${[Z]_1^N}^{(j \to r)}$ the vector which is equal to $[Z]_1^N$ in all coordinates except on coordinate $j$, where $Z_j = r$. Using eq. \ref{k_is_zero_eq}, we get: $$ F_{N+1}^{\vec{k}^{(1)}}([\epsilon]_1^{N+1}) = \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_3^{k_2} \dots \partial \epsilon_{N+1}^{k_N}} \left[ \left. \frac{\partial F_{N+1}}{\partial \epsilon_2} \right|_{\epsilon_2 = 0} \right] \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = $$ $$ \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_3^{k_2} \dots \partial \epsilon_{N+1}^{k_N}} \Biggl\{ - \sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} \sum_{[Z]_1^{N+1}} $$ $$ \left[ P({[Z]_1^{N+1}}^{(2 \to r)}) \log P(Z_{N+1} | [Z]_1^{N}) - \right. $$ $$ \left. \left. \left. P(Z_{N+1} | [Z]_1^{N}) P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(2 \to r)}) \right] \right|_{\epsilon_2 = 0} \Biggr\} \right|_{[\epsilon]_1^{N+1} = 0} = $$ $$ \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_2^{k_2} \dots \partial \epsilon_{N}^{k_N}} \Biggl\{ - \sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} \sum_{[Z]_1^{N}} $$ $$ \left[ P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(1 \to r)}) \log P(Z_{N} | [Z]_1^{N-1}) - \right. $$ \begin{equation} \left. \left. \left. P(Z_{N} | [Z]_1^{N-1}) P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(1 \to r)}) \right] \right|_{\epsilon_1 = 0} \Biggr\} \right|_{[\epsilon]_1^{N} = 0} = F_{N}^{\vec{k}}([\epsilon]_1^{N})\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Cases $k_1=0$ (blocking lemma at the zero site) and $k_1=1$ (differentiate once in $\epsilon_2$, reducing to $k_1=0$).
nodes.label: zero_tail_lemma

nodes.name: Case k_1 = 0
nodes.statement: \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})} F_{N}([\epsilon]_{r+1}^{N+r})}{\partial \epsilon_{r+2}^{k_2},..,\partial \epsilon_{r+N}^{k_N}} \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = F_N^{\vec{k}}([\epsilon]_{r+1}^{r+N})
nodes.label: k_is_zero_eq

nodes.name: Case k_1 = 1
nodes.statement: \left. \left. \left. P(Z_{N} | [Z]_1^{N-1}) P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(1 \to r)}) \right] \right|_{\epsilon_1 = 0} \Biggr\} \right|_{[\epsilon]_1^{N} = 0} = F_{N}^{\vec{k}}([\epsilon]_1^{N})

nodes.name: Case k_1 = 0 via the blocking lemma
nodes.statement: Assume first $k_1 = 0$. Using lemma \ref{F_cond_lemma}, we get: $$ F_{N+r}^{\vec{k}^{(r)}}([\epsilon]_1^{N+r}) = \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k}^{(r)})} F_{r+N}([\epsilon]_1^{N+r})}{\partial \epsilon_{r+2}^{k_2},..,\partial \epsilon_{r+N}^{k_N}} \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = $$ \begin{equation} \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})} F_{N}([\epsilon]_{r+1}^{N+r})}{\partial \epsilon_{r+2}^{k_2},..,\partial \epsilon_{r+N}^{k_N}} \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = F_N^{\vec{k}}([\epsilon]_{r+1}^{r+N}) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Case k_1 = 0 via the blocking lemma

nodes.name: Case k_1 = 1
nodes.statement: The case $k_1 = 1$ is reduced back to the case $k_1=0$ by taking the derivative. We denote ${[Z]_1^N}^{(j \to r)}$ the vector which is equal to $[Z]_1^N$ in all coordinates except on coordinate $j$, where $Z_j = r$. Using eq. \ref{k_is_zero_eq}, we get: $$ F_{N+1}^{\vec{k}^{(1)}}([\epsilon]_1^{N+1}) = \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_3^{k_2} \dots \partial \epsilon_{N+1}^{k_N}} \left[ \left. \frac{\partial F_{N+1}}{\partial \epsilon_2} \right|_{\epsilon_2 = 0} \right] \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = $$ $$ \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_3^{k_2} \dots \partial \epsilon_{N+1}^{k_N}} \Biggl\{ - \sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} \sum_{[Z]_1^{N+1}} $$ $$ \left[ P({[Z]_1^{N+1}}^{(2 \to r)}) \log P(Z_{N+1} | [Z]_1^{N}) - \right. $$ $$ \left. \left. \left. P(Z_{N+1} | [Z]_1^{N}) P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(2 \to r)}) \right] \right|_{\epsilon_2 = 0} \Biggr\} \right|_{[\epsilon]_1^{N+1} = 0} = $$ $$ \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_2^{k_2} \dots \partial \epsilon_{N}^{k_N}} \Biggl\{ - \sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} \sum_{[Z]_1^{N}} $$ $$ \left[ P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(1 \to r)}) \log P(Z_{N} | [Z]_1^{N-1}) - \right. $$ \begin{equation} \left. \left. \left. P(Z_{N} | [Z]_1^{N-1}) P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(1 \to r)}) \right] \right|_{\epsilon_1 = 0} \Biggr\} \right|_{[\epsilon]_1^{N} = 0} = F_{N}^{\vec{k}}([\epsilon]_1^{N})\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Case k_1 = 1

nodes.name: Reduce k_1 = 1 to k_1 = 0 by differentiating
nodes.statement: The case $k_1 = 1$ is reduced back to the case $k_1=0$ by taking the derivative.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce k_1 = 1 to k_1 = 0 by differentiating

nodes.name: Differentiate in epsilon_2 and apply the k_1 = 0 case
nodes.statement: We denote ${[Z]_1^N}^{(j \to r)}$ the vector which is equal to $[Z]_1^N$ in all coordinates except on coordinate $j$, where $Z_j = r$. Using eq. \ref{k_is_zero_eq}, we get: $$ F_{N+1}^{\vec{k}^{(1)}}([\epsilon]_1^{N+1}) = \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_3^{k_2} \dots \partial \epsilon_{N+1}^{k_N}} \left[ \left. \frac{\partial F_{N+1}}{\partial \epsilon_2} \right|_{\epsilon_2 = 0} \right] \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = $$ $$ \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_3^{k_2} \dots \partial \epsilon_{N+1}^{k_N}} \Biggl\{ - \sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} \sum_{[Z]_1^{N+1}} $$ $$ \left[ P({[Z]_1^{N+1}}^{(2 \to r)}) \log P(Z_{N+1} | [Z]_1^{N}) - \right. $$ $$ \left. \left. \left. P(Z_{N+1} | [Z]_1^{N}) P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(2 \to r)}) \right] \right|_{\epsilon_2 = 0} \Biggr\} \right|_{[\epsilon]_1^{N+1} = 0} = $$ $$ \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_2^{k_2} \dots \partial \epsilon_{N}^{k_N}} \Biggl\{ - \sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} \sum_{[Z]_1^{N}} $$ $$ \left[ P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(1 \to r)}) \log P(Z_{N} | [Z]_1^{N-1}) - \right. $$ \begin{equation} \left. \left. \left. P(Z_{N} | [Z]_1^{N-1}) P({[Z]_1^{N}}^{(1 \to r)}) \right] \right|_{\epsilon_1 = 0} \Biggr\} \right|_{[\epsilon]_1^{N} = 0} = F_{N}^{\vec{k}}([\epsilon]_1^{N})\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate in epsilon_2 and apply the k_1 = 0 case

nodes.name: Taylor coefficient as a sum of mixed derivatives
nodes.statement: \noindent $C_N^{(k)}$ is obtained by summing $F_N^{\vec{k}}$ on all $\vec{k}$'s with weight $k$: \begin{equation} C_N^{(k)} = \sum_{\vec{k},\omega(\vec{k})=k} F_N^{\vec{k}} \end{equation}

nodes.name: C_N^(k) as sum over weight-k vectors
nodes.statement: C_N^{(k)} = \sum_{\vec{k},\omega(\vec{k})=k} F_N^{\vec{k}}

nodes.name: No-hole lemma
nodes.statement_short: $F_N^{\vec k}$ vanishes if some site $i$ with $k_i\ge1$ is followed (before $N$) by a site $j$ with $k_j\le1$.

nodes.name: Proof of the no-hole lemma
nodes.statement_short: Case $k_j=0$: blocking removes $\epsilon_i$. Case $k_j=1$: the first derivative in $\epsilon_j$ at 0, computed via Bayes' rule and blocking, does not involve $\epsilon_i$.
nodes.label: No_hole_strong_lemma

nodes.name: Case k_j = 0 vanishes
nodes.statement: \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_1^{k_1},.., \partial \epsilon_i^{k_i-1},.., \partial \epsilon_N^{k_N}} \left[\left. \frac{\partial F_{N-j+1}([\epsilon]_j^N)}{\partial \epsilon_i} \right] \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = 0

nodes.name: Probability of Z as sum over X
nodes.statement: \sum_{[X]_1^N} P([X]_1^N) \prod_{i=1}^N (\delta_{X_i Z_i} + \epsilon_i t_{X_i Z_i})

nodes.name: Derivative of P(Z) in epsilon_j
nodes.statement: \left. \left\{ \sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} P({[Z]_1^N}^{(j \to r)}) \right\} \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0}

nodes.name: Derivative of conditional probability
nodes.statement: \left. \left. P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1} ) P({[Z]_1^{N-1}}^{(j \to r)}) \right] \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0}

nodes.name: Derivative of P log P
nodes.statement: \left. \left. P({[Z]_1^N}^{(j \to r)}) - P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1}) P({[Z]_1^{N-1}}^{(j \to r)})\right\} \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0}

nodes.name: Derivative of F_N in epsilon_j
nodes.statement: \left. \left. P(Z_N | [Z]_j^{N-1}) P({[Z]_j^{N-1}}^{(1 \to r)}) \right] \Biggr\} \right|_{\epsilon_1 = 0}
nodes.label: F_N_deriv_eq

nodes.name: Case k_j = 0 via the blocking lemma
nodes.statement: Assume first $k_j = 0$. Using lemma \ref{F_cond_lemma} we get $$ F_N^{\vec{k}} \equiv \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})} F_N(\vec{\epsilon})}{\partial \epsilon_1^{k_1},..,\partial \epsilon_N^{k_N}} \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = \left. \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})} F_{N-j+1}([\epsilon]_j^N)}{\partial \epsilon_1^{k_1},..,\partial \epsilon_N^{k_N}} \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = $$ \begin{equation} \frac{\partial^{\omega(\vec{k})-1}}{\partial \epsilon_1^{k_1},.., \partial \epsilon_i^{k_i-1},.., \partial \epsilon_N^{k_N}} \left[\left. \frac{\partial F_{N-j+1}([\epsilon]_j^N)}{\partial \epsilon_i} \right] \right|_{\vec{\epsilon} = 0} = 0 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Case k_j = 0 via the blocking lemma

nodes.name: Case k_j = 1
nodes.statement_short: Case k_j = 1

nodes.name: Write P(Z) as a sum over hidden states
nodes.statement: Assume now $k_j = 1$. Write the probability of $Z$: $$ P([Z]_1^N) = \sum_{[X]_1^N} P([X]_1^N) P([Z]_1^N | [X]_1^N) = $$ \begin{equation} \sum_{[X]_1^N} P([X]_1^N) \prod_{i=1}^N (\delta_{X_i Z_i} + \epsilon_i t_{X_i Z_i})\end{equation} \noindent where $\delta$ is Kronecker's delta.
nodes.statement_short: Write P(Z) as a sum over hidden states

nodes.name: Differentiate P(Z) in epsilon_j
nodes.statement: Differentiate with respect to $\epsilon_j$: $$ \left. \frac{\partial P([Z]_1^N)}{\partial \epsilon_j} \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0} = $$ $$ \left. \sum_{[X]_1^N} \left[ P([X]_1^N) t_{X_j Z_j} \prod_{i \neq j} (\delta_{X_i Z_i} + \epsilon_i t_{X_i Z_i}) \right] \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0} = $$ \begin{equation} \left. \left\{ \sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} P({[Z]_1^N}^{(j \to r)}) \right\} \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate P(Z) in epsilon_j

nodes.name: Bayes' rule gives the derivative of the conditional probability
nodes.statement: Using Bayes' rule $P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1}) = \frac{P([Z]_1^N)}{P([Z]_1^{N-1})}$, we get: $$ \left. \frac{\partial P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1})}{\partial \epsilon_j} \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0} = $$ $$ \frac{1}{P([Z]_1^{N-1})} \sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} \left[ P({[Z]_1^N}^{(j \to r)}) - \right. $$ \begin{equation} \left. \left. P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1} ) P({[Z]_1^{N-1}}^{(j \to r)}) \right] \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bayes' rule gives the derivative of the conditional probability

nodes.name: Derivative of P log P
nodes.statement: This gives: $$ \left. \frac{\partial [P([Z]_1^N) \log P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1})]}{\partial \epsilon_j} \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0} = $$ $$ \sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} \left\{ P({[Z]_1^N}^{(j \to r)}) \log P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1}) + \right. $$ \begin{equation} \left. \left. P({[Z]_1^N}^{(j \to r)}) - P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1}) P({[Z]_1^{N-1}}^{(j \to r)})\right\} \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Derivative of P log P

nodes.name: Derivative of F_N, then blocking
nodes.statement: And therefore: $$ \left. \frac{\partial F_N}{\partial \epsilon_j} \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0} = $$ $$ -\sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} \Biggl\{ \sum_{[Z]_1^N} \left[ P({[Z]_1^N}^{(j \to r)}) \log P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1}) - \right. $$ $$ \left. \left. P(Z_N | [Z]_1^{N-1}) P({[Z]_1^{N-1}}^{(j \to r)}) \right] \Biggr\} \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0} = $$ $$ \Biggl\{ -\sum_{r=1}^{s} t_{X_i r} \sum_{[Z]_j^N} \left[ P({[Z]_j^N}^{(1 \to r)}) \log P(Z_N | [Z]_j^{N-1}) - \right. $$ \begin{equation} \left. \left. P(Z_N | [Z]_j^{N-1}) P({[Z]_j^{N-1}}^{(1 \to r)}) \right] \Biggr\} \right|_{\epsilon_1 = 0} \end{equation} \noindent The latter equality comes from using eq. \ref{blocking_cond}, which 'blocks' the dependence backwards.
nodes.statement_short: Derivative of F_N, then blocking

nodes.name: epsilon_i absent for i < j, so the mixed derivative vanishes
nodes.statement: Eq. \ref{F_N_deriv_eq} shows that $\epsilon_i$ does not appear in $\left. \frac{\partial F_N}{\partial \epsilon_j} \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0}$ for $i < j$, therefore $\left. \frac{\partial^{k_i+1} F_N}{\partial \epsilon_i^{k_i} \partial \epsilon_j} \right|_{\epsilon_j = 0} = 0$ and $F_N^{\vec{k}} = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: epsilon_i absent for i < j, so the mixed derivative vanishes

nodes.name: Proof of the main theorem
nodes.statement_short: Only vectors of bounded 'length' contribute (no-hole lemma); trimming leading zeros (zero-tail lemma) makes $C_N^{(k)}$ constant in $N$, and analyticity identifies it with $C^{(k)}$.
nodes.label: strong_thm

nodes.name: F_N^k reduces to a vector of length ceil((k+3)/2)
nodes.statement: F_N^{\vec{k}} = F_{\lceil \frac{k+3}{2} \rceil}^{(k_{N-\lceil \frac{k+3}{2} \rceil+1},..,{k_N})}

nodes.name: Introduce the length of k
nodes.statement: Let $\vec{k} = [k]_1^N$ with $\omega(\vec{k}) = k$. Define its 'length' as $l(\vec{k}) = N+1-\min_{k_i > 1} \{i \}$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the length of k

nodes.name: No-hole lemma bounds the length of contributing k
nodes.statement: It easily follows from lemma \ref{No_hole_strong_lemma} that $F_N^{\vec{k}} \neq 0 \Rightarrow l(\vec{k}) \leq \lceil \frac{k+3}{2} \rceil - 1$.
nodes.statement_short: No-hole lemma bounds the length of contributing k

nodes.name: Zero-tail lemma reduces each term to fixed length
nodes.statement: Thus, according to lemma \ref{zero_tail_lemma}: \begin{equation} F_N^{\vec{k}} = F_{\lceil \frac{k+3}{2} \rceil}^{(k_{N-\lceil \frac{k+3}{2} \rceil+1},..,{k_N})} \end{equation} \noindent for all $\vec{k}$'s in the sum.
nodes.statement_short: Zero-tail lemma reduces each term to fixed length

nodes.name: Sum over weight k: C_N^(k) constant in N
nodes.statement: Summing on all $F_N^{\vec{k}}$ with the same 'weight' gives $C_N^{(k)} = C_{\lceil \frac{k+3}{2} \rceil}^{(k)}, \: \forall N > \lceil \frac{k+3}{2} \rceil$.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over weight k: C_N^(k) constant in N

nodes.name: Analyticity gives the limit C^(k)
nodes.statement: But from the analyticity of $C_N$ and $\bar{H}$ near $\epsilon=0$ it follows that $\lim_{N \to \infty} C_N^{(k)} = C^{(k)}$, therefore $C_N^{(k)} = C^{(k)}, \: \forall N \geq \lceil \frac{k+3}{2} \rceil $. \\
nodes.statement_short: Analyticity gives the limit C^(k)

nodes.name: Weaker settling for conditional-probability functionals
nodes.statement: For other functions involving only conditional probabilities (e.g. relative entropy between two {\it HMPs}) a weaker result holds: the coefficients 'settle' for $N \geq k$.
assumptions: For other functions involving only conditional probabilities (e.g. relative entropy between two {\it HMPs})

nodes.name: Settling in the almost-memoryless regime
nodes.statement: As it turns out, exactly the same 'settling' as was proven in Thm. \ref{main_thm} happens in the 'almost memoryless' regime, where $M$ is close to a matrix which makes the $X_i$'s i.i.d.
assumptions: the 'almost memoryless' regime, where $M$ is close to a matrix which makes the $X_i$'s i.i.d
conclusions: exactly the same 'settling' as was proven in Thm. \ref{main_thm} happens
